chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated, saying: Al-Husayn ibn Aban narrated, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: I asked him: 'Has Allah always been the Willer?' He replied: 'Indeed, the Willer is not [called such] except for a Will that is with Him; rather, He has always been All-Knowing, All-Powerful, then He intended.'
ai.seo_question: Is God's Will an eternal attribute or an action?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this narration to articulate the Ash'ari-leaning Shia view that Divine Will (Irādah) is an action (fi'l) rather than an eternal attribute (sifah), distinguishing it from Knowledge and Power. By stating God was 'Knowing and Powerful, then Willed,' the Imam emphasizes that Will is contingent upon the object of will, thereby avoiding the implication of an eternal, independent will co-existing with the Divine Essence.
